brief: JPMorgan's Joyce Chang reports takeaways from pre-Jackson Hole seminars and the G20 meeting, framed by her Six Ds thesis (deficits, deregulation, de-carbonization, de-population, de-globalization, de-dollarization) that forces regime change toward higher rates, volatility and risk premium, with duration pain coexisting alongside equity gains. The chain runs: Warsh is prepared to hike, JPM economics still looks for December while an earlier move is not unreasonable, and August employment and CPI decide that meeting. Long-term yields stay unanchored without fiscal action, because the FY26 deficit is projected near $2.1trn or 6.5% of GDP and net interest doubles from about $1trn to $2.1trn by 2035. Treasury ownership shifts, falling FX reserves and AI capex crowding out (high grade AI issuance $266bn YTD versus $139bn for all of 2025) add term premium, implying a 5.5% nominal 10yr target on 2.5% real yields and 3% expected inflation. AI investment, $6.7trn globally by 2030, fuses market with economic risk since US market cap is 248% of GDP, and interwar precedent says booms of 2-4% of GDP end in rupture, not soft landings. Middle powers reject winner-takes-all framing and the G20 ended without a communique.
